title: Authentic Goan Vindaloo Paste
description: A fiery, traditional Goan masala paste driven by toasted whole spices, pungent garlic, roasted fenugreek, and sharp vinegar.

ingredients.notes: Dried: stems removed (gives vibrant deep red colour and fruity body)
stems removed; provides aggressive, lingering heat (found at any Indian grocer)
whole seeds, dry-roasted until lightly golden
Brown Or Black: classic Goan pairing with fenugreek
crushed into small shards to protect grinder
Or Malt Vinegar: traditional acidic base; replace lemon juice

method.instruction: Place the crushed cinnamon shards, cardamom pods, cloves, black peppercorns, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and dried chillies into a dry skillet over low heat.

Toast gently for 90–120 seconds, stirring constantly, until the fenugreek turns lightly golden and the spices release a rich, sweet, and pungent aroma. Immediately transfer to a plate to stop cooking.

Once cooled, transfer the toasted spices to a spice grinder and pulse until finely ground. Pass the ground mixture through a fine wire mesh sieve to remove any fibrous cardamom husks or woody cinnamon fragments.

Add the sieved spice blend, fresh ginger, garlic cloves, and vinegar into a small blender or food processor. Blend into a smooth, thick, deep-crimson paste, adding 1–2 tablespoons of water only if needed to loosen.

notes.title: Toasting Fenugreek
notes.content: Keep heat strictly on low/medium-low when dry roasting. Fenugreek seeds turn harsh and aggressively bitter if blackened. Pull them the moment they turn amber-golden.

notes.title: Vinegar Varieties
notes.content: Authentic Goan vindaloo relies on palm toddy vinegar. Apple cider vinegar, malt vinegar, or red wine vinegar provide the closest authentic tang. Avoid plain white vinegar if possible.

notes.title: Chilli Selection
notes.content: Never omit the Kashmiri chillies—they build the signature ruby color and sauce thickness. For serious heat, swap the secondary dried chillies for 1–2 dried Bhut Jolokia (Ghost Pepper) or fresh habanero peppers.
